messages:
Aisha Rahman: Quick postmortem follow-up: two regressions slipped past our canary cohorts. We discussed fixes in the retro; putting owners/timelines here so they're actionable.
Tom Becker: I'll own the automated rollback tiers + safe pause flow. Plan: implement a three-tier rule set (soft, hard, emergency) and a single idempotent API endpoint `POST /rollouts/{id}/action` that accepts `pause|throttle|rollback`. PoC by Fri.
Jun Park: I'll own flag metadata + enforcement. Proposal: require `max_blast_radius` + `probe_fraction` and add a server-side pre-merge lint. I'll draft schema and a CLI warning.
Leah O'Neill: I'll handle telemetry, baselining, and recurrence detection. I'll add a daily canary anomaly job and a monthly pattern report to identify slow drifts. Backfill 60 days for priors.
Aisha Rahman: Good. Please drop PR links here and update the runbook with owners + expected dates. We'll have a weekly 30m sync for 6 weeks to keep momentum.
Tom Becker: Implementation notes: soft trigger -> throttle to 0.1% and collect 15m extra signal; hard trigger -> pause rollout; emergency -> full rollback. Each action should create an audit event and notify owners. Also add a cooldown to prevent flip-flops.
Jun Park: Schema sketch I'll propose:

```yaml
flag:
  name: string
  owner: string
  max_blast_radius: float # required
  probe_fraction: float # fraction used to gather signal
  ramp_policy: list[float]
  require_review: bool
```

I'll add a pre-commit CLI lint and a CI gate that fails if `max_blast_radius` missing. Default probe_fraction for experiments = 0.005.
Leah O'Neill: Detection queries planned: `canary_short_spike` (error-rate > 3x baseline in 10m), `canary_latency_shift` (p95 +30% sustained 20m), and `cohort_drift` (slow rise across cohorts over 48h). Alerts to #eng-oncall and the primary owner.
Aisha Rahman: Owner/timeline matrix: Tom -> rollback engine (PoC Fri, tests next Tue), Jun -> flag schema + lint (PR Thu), Leah -> telemetry jobs + backfill (jobs Mon). I'll update the postmortem and runbook with this matrix.
guardrail-bot: Event: "Rollout-safety weekly check" scheduled Tue 09:30, recurring 6x.
Tom Becker: PoC will call `POST /rollouts/{id}/action` with payload `{action: "throttle", fraction: 0.001, reason: "canary_soft_trigger"}`. Will keep actions idempotent and instrumented.
Jun Park: I'll add a server-side enforcement so new flags without `max_blast_radius` are blocked with the message: "Add max_blast_radius to proceed (recommended 0.02 for experiments)". Also adding a UI hint for owners.
Leah O'Neill: I'll backfill 60 days and run an initial historical sweep to find any recurring patterns; will add a dashboard and a weekly regression digest emailed to primary owners.
Aisha Rahman: One procedural change: rotate remediation primary monthly and keep a named backup. Add that to the runbook and to the flag metadata.
Tom Becker: Also proposing a low-noise long-term probe: deterministic 0.25% traffic slice that persists across deploys to measure baseline stability. That should reduce noisy false positives.
Jun Park: Adding `probe_fraction` to the flag schema covers that. We'll mark those probes in telemetry so Leah can use them as control cohorts.
Leah O'Neill: I'll wire controls in the dashboards. Saved queries and dashboard links will be posted in #eng-observability once ready.
Aisha Rahman: Please react with :white_check_mark: when you open your first PR. I'll lock the action items in the postmortem and track them in the follow-up calendar.
Tom Becker: Opened draft PR for rollback PoC: https://git.redwood/ri/guardrails/pulls/688 (WIP).
Jun Park: Draft PR for flag schema + pre-merge lint: https://git.redwood/ri/flags/pulls/210 (WIP).
Leah O'Neill: Backfill started; will post dashboards in #eng-observability and ping this thread.
Aisha Rahman: Thanks all. If anyone hits blockers, ping me. Let's aim to close the high-priority items within 2 sprints and iterate on thresholds after we have baselines.
Tom Becker: Noted.
Jun Park: Noted.
Leah O'Neill: Noted.
Aisha Rahman: Closing note: we agreed to treat recurring patterns as first-class workstreams with explicit owners and a monthly review. That should cut down on regression churn.
